title: Ticket lifecycle and flows
idea: The ticket lifecycle is a small state machine: a Ticket starts ACTIVE and may only move along allowed arrows to PAID, LOST or EXITED.
points: ACTIVE becomes PAID after payment, or LOST when an attendant reports it.
PAID becomes EXITED at the gate, or ACTIVE again after the grace window.
A ParkingSpot goes FREE to OCCUPIED at entry and back to FREE at exit.
Illegal moves are refused in one place, the enum, not in every gate.

messages.label: arrive KA01AB1234
messages.note: A car reaches entry gate IN-1. The gate reads the vehicle type.

messages.label: park(vehicle)
messages.note: The lot picks a spot. The spot goes FREE to OCCUPIED, and ticket T-1 starts ACTIVE.

messages.label: T-1 at F1-C1
messages.note: The gate prints the ticket and lifts the barrier.

messages.label: pay(T-1)
messages.note: At the pay station the lot prices the stay. Page 3 merged pay and exit; here they are separate steps.

messages.label: charge(15000)
messages.note: The lot charges the fee once, in paise.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: Success moves T-1 from ACTIVE to PAID. A grace window to reach the exit starts now.

messages.label: scan T-1
messages.note: The driver reaches exit gate OUT-1 and scans the ticket.

messages.label: exit(T-1)
messages.note: PAID moves to EXITED and the spot goes back to FREE. An ACTIVE ticket is refused here.

messages.label: barrier up
messages.note: If the grace window had run out, T-1 would be ACTIVE again and owe more.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Ticket asks the enum and throws on an illegal move.

walk.text: T-1 takes the happy path: pay, then exit.
T-2 tries to leave without paying.
T-3 is reported lost, then paid with the flat fee.
T-4 pays but overstays the grace window; then T-1 tries to pay again.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states for each state.
`moveTo` is the only way to change status, and it refuses illegal moves.

pitfalls: Never set `status` directly from a gate; every change goes through `moveTo`.
Keep ticket and spot states separate; an EXITED ticket must also free its spot.
Decide the grace window rule up front, or paid drivers get stuck at the exit.

quiz.q: What does the line for T-2 print?
options: Nothing; the exception stops the program
quiz.why: ACTIVE allows only PAID and LOST. `moveTo` throws, and `step` catches it and prints the refused move with the current state.

takeaway: Write allowed ticket moves once, in the enum, and refuse the rest.

starters: Should a failed payment be its own ticket state?
How long should the grace window be, and who sets it?
Would the State pattern fit better than an enum here?
